summary.text: Father of the Maeonian captains Mesthles (`mesthles-maeonian`) and Antiphus (`antiphus-maeonian`) — attested by Homer in the Catalogue of Ships and by Apollodorus among the allies who joined the Trojans.

story.text: Homer's muster-roll sets Mesthles and Antiphus, sons twain of Talaemenes, at the head of the Maeonians whose birth was beneath Tmolas; their mother was the nymph of the Gygaean lake.
Apollodorus, listing the allies who came to Troy after nine years of siege, makes Mesthles and Antiphus sons of Talaemenes among the Maeonian captains.
